chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Khallad al-Sindi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) was saying regarding the man who dies and leaves wealth, and there is no one for him: 'Give the inheritance to his city folk'.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the inheritance of a person who dies with no heirs?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) designates the 'hamsharijah'—interpreted by Shia scholars as the city's inhabitants or those sharing the same social and geographic community—as the residual heirs when no direct lineage exists. This ruling establishes a precedent for communal inheritance (*al-muwattha*) in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that wealth remains within the local social fabric rather than reverting to the state or treasury. The term 'hamsharijah' highlights the importance of social cohesion and shared identity in Islamic inheritance law.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Khallad Al Sindy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying regarding the man who died and left wealth, and there was no one for him: ‘Give the inheritance to his city folk’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Khallad al-Sindiy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
’Amir al-Mu’minin would say, ‘If a man dies without leaving behind any heirs then give his legacy to Hamshahrijah (his fellow countryman)
